subdivision.heading: Joining and Separating Claims and Parties

operative_text.controlling:
3.69(1)  A party may join 2 or more claims in an action unless the
Court otherwise orders.
(2)  A party may sue or be sued in different capacities in the same
action.
(3)  If there is more than one defendant or respondent, it is not
necessary for each to have an interest
(a) in all the remedies claimed or sought, or
(b) in each claim included in the action.

BOOK_B.title: Joining claims

commentary.text: Rule 3.69 See Alberta Rules of Court, Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 3.69. 1. Permissive Nature of Rule Rule 32 allows a plaintiff to unite several causes of action in one action. However it does not require him to do so. Bank of Nova Scotia v. Guenette (1986), 75 A.R. 361 at 368 (Master). One action may contain alternative claims based on different causes of action. See Elliott v. Barry (1920), 15 Alta. L.R. 329 (C.A.). Also, Hyndman J.A. said: I had thought that there was no doubt about the right to rely upon and claim several different rights “alternatively although they may be inconsistent”… … the plaintiff may claim alternative remedies and is not put to his election until his right to relief is established either after default of defence when he may prove for judgment, or after the evidence is concluded on a trial. Campbell v. Munro (1922), 17 Alta. L.R. 272 at 275, 276 (C.A.). Where a plaintiff was suing in contract on six separate invoices, including interest charges, Master Funduk stated: I have already concluded that each is a separate contract. The plaintiff is uniting six causes of action in this action, which is permissible: R. 32. Satelite Painting Enterprises Ltd. v. Yukon Trailer Service Ltd. (1992), 85 Alta. L.R. (2d) 328 at 331 (Master).
